title: Giving

screens.title: Lesson 7: Giving, an idea for later
screens.text: Some people choose to give. Our family does not do this yet, so this is just to learn what giving means. Press Start when you are ready.

art.alt: A gift and a helping hand

screens.text: Giving means letting some of our money go to help someone else. When money is given, it leaves, just like a swipe. It is gone from us, and someone else has it.

art.alt: Money leaves a hand and goes to help someone

screens.text: People give in different ways: a gift for a friend, a donation to help others, or time and help. Time and help do not cost any money at all.

art.alt: A gift, a donation, and time and help

screens.text: Here is a pretend example. Someone has 20 dollars on a card and gives 5 dollars. Their account goes down to 15 dollars, just like a swipe. Someone else gets 5 dollars of help.

art.alt: Pretend: give 5 dollars by card, the account goes from 20 dollars to 15 dollars

screens.prompt: In the pretend example, someone has 20 dollars and gives 5 dollars. How much do they have left?

options.label: 25 dollars
options.why: Giving takes money away, so there is less, not more. 20 take away 5 is 15.

options.label: 15 dollars
options.why: Yes. 20 take away 5 is 15. Giving is money leaving, like a swipe.

options.label: 5 dollars
options.why: 5 dollars is what was given. What is left is 20 take away 5, which is 15.

options.label: No. Giving is a choice. Each family decides if and when.
options.why: Yes. There is no rule. Our family might talk about it later, and that is fine.

options.label: Yes, every day.
options.why: No one has to give. It is a choice a family makes, when it is ready.

options.label: Only grown-ups can think about it.
options.why: Kids can learn what giving means too. That is all we are doing today.

screens.text: Giving does not always mean money. Time and help are gifts too: helping a neighbor, sharing a toy, or making a card for someone.

art.alt: Helping, sharing and making a card

options.label: Buying a toy.
options.why: Buying a toy costs money. A gift of help costs only our time.

options.label: Swiping a card.
options.why: A swipe costs real money, so it is not a free gift.

options.label: Helping a neighbor carry groceries.
options.why: Yes. Time and help are real gifts, and they cost no money.

talk.q: What did you learn giving means?
talk.note: Money leaving to help someone, like a swipe; or time and help, which cost nothing. Your family does not give money yet, and there is nothing to decide today.

talk.q: Can you think of a time someone helped you, with no money at all?
talk.note: A gentle way to talk about time and help.

talk.q: If a child pressed Ask a grown-up in this lesson, what was the question?
talk.note: Common ones: "Do we give?" (not yet; maybe a topic for later) and who gets the money. You decide what to say about your own family’s values.
